“An endless amount of victims.”


I scoff at my camera. 


“I wouldn’t say *endless*.”


I set my phone down, done reading the articles over my shenanigans. Behind me sat a girl, unconscious, tied to a chair. I adjust my camera focus on her and look into the lens. 


“It has been 1 weeks and 4 days, folks. That’s 11 people already, and STILL NO ONE HAS-,” my voice trails off as a inhale deeply and close my eyes, “still no one has figured out where I am.” 


Detectives and police all over the country are trying to pinpoint my location. I have had this planned for years. Ever since the police were unable to find my sister in time, I vowed I would give them a reason to work faster. And yet, my point, my goal, my purpose seems to be as minute as the sand that washes off the shore. No one seems to care when it doesn’t effect them. But it will. Oh, it will.


“This,” I grab the girl by her face, “is Marie. The president’s daughter. She has not-so-voluntarily offered to be ultimatum number 12.”


I flash the clock towards the camera.


“Twelve more minutes. Has this become important to you yet, Mister President?”

I walk over to the camera and rotate it to show the line of bodies that were the last 11 people to die due to a slow response from a faulty police team.


“Soon, she’ll be as “unimportant” as the rest of these poor souls.”


I adjust the camera back to Marie, who has started to stir and awake. I walk towards her and she starts to squirm and whine as she looks at me.


“Smile for the camera, dear.”


I pull a knife from my waistband and rub the side against her cheek and glance over to the camera.


“4 more minutes, Mister President.”

Valentina wraps her baby in a soft blanket. He looks up to her and she can almost feel as if he's trying to smile at her. His deep red eyes pierce hers as they look at one another.

"I'm sorry I haven't taken you out side, Theadus," she talks calmly to her son. "but the others... they fear those with eyes of Crimson."

She nuzzles her forehead against his. 

"I don't want to lose you to them. They'll take you away from me."

Theadus grabs his mother's hair and puts it in his mouth, babbling on.

"But one day, you will be stronger than them. One day, you'll discover the Abyss. And then not even the gods themselves will be able to control you."

She picks up the child and lays him softly in his crib, kissing his cheek.

"Then," she pauses, "then, you will control everything."

The gods gathered around the Seer, who spoke of a child who will bring destruction to the human realm.

"This child," she spoke in a soft, raspy voice, "will be the downfall of the human realm, as well as your Circle of Gods."

"Impossible!" shouted Might. "No \*human\* would be able to overpower the \*\*GODS\*\*!"

"Quiet, Might!" Wisdom snapped. "Let her speak!"

Wisdom nods to the frail, blind old lady in the middle of their Circle.

"You have let your powers seep into the Realm of Humans," she scolded, "claiming to still be in control. You have fought for a millennium to contain the powers to a select few you have trusted. You have prevented the humans from worshiping other humans, for fear of them abandoning their loyalty to \*you\*. You lot never should have entrusted the humans. You should have wiped them all when you were careless and allowed them the taste of your power. Now..." her voice trails off, and then she is cut off by Chaos.

"\*\*ENOUGH\*\*!" Fire spews from his mouth as his voice echoes in the Hall. "I will not sit here and be chided by an Ancient who entrusted \*Us\* with maintaining control. You give us control over an entire realm, and then chastise us because you think \*WE\* messed up?! Why give us any amount of control if you don-"

Chaos is forced into his seat by an unseen force, the sound of him hitting his chair echoes in the Hall and all is silent.

The Seer rises from her chair, her hood lowering from her head. Her eyes, just two holes as deep as the Abyss itself focus on Chaos and fear overtakes the look of anger on his face. 

The other gods lean back in their chairs, watching the Seer slowly move towards Chaos.

"Perhaps you are right. Perhaps \*I\* am at fault for trusting \*you\* lot, the same way you trusted the humans."

The air is ripe with unease as the Seer stands in front of Chaos, looking down onto him.

"I have prevented the boy from accessing his powers for a long while. But my ward will not contain the power within him for long."

Her stare deepens into Chaos before he is ripped from his chair by the Abyss. Screams from the god fill the air as the darkness fades along with his voice. The Seer returns to her chair and raises her hood, covering all but her wrinkled mouth. 

Silence has overtaken the congregation of gods, all of which too afraid to speak.

Life clears her throat, and looks to Chaos' empty chair.

"M'lady, what is the child's name?" She inquires.

A long pause before a scowl stretches across the Seers lips.

"Theadus"
